CSharpDecisions: TryResolveDirectParallelTarget accepts only one callback expression: a direct flow from the role name to a resolved synchronous user function; additional arguments must be other name bindings. EmitDirectParallelCallback also requires exact input/result types.

The general path binds the current role item, emits all preceding statements, evaluates the final expression, stores the mapped result, drops callback locals and restores enclosing locals per iteration.
SLGObservedDifferences: Entry and ordinary-function sequential paths already contain structured role materialization and emitRegion fallback, but the control-region sequential path unconditionally renders the terminal node as a function target.

emitRegionState classifies only kind19/20 ancestors as nested region boundaries. Parallel callback descendants therefore also enter the enclosing region order. Existing special handling separates a callback-rooted region from its source, but not from an enclosing region.

parallelUsesComputePool and three sequential paths select by terminal call identity without proving the entire callback is one direct expression. A preceding effect followed by a function call must remain part of the general body.
ASTObservation: Actual current CLI ast-nodes observations show direct callback children source-read, target Path and one expression-statement root; effect-call adds a second expression root. No extra callback BlockBody AST survives flattening. Records: parallel12414-ast/*.execution.json.
plannedRepair: Create one shared direct-body classification using selected user declaration, exact role/additional-name arguments and complete direct AST child set, then consume it in compute-pool admission and all three sequential paths.
Make control-region general callback emission reuse existing structured role materialization and emitRegion inside the mapping loop.

Keep nested callback-owned IR out of enclosing region schedules, while a callback-rooted or nested control region admits exactly its own callback owner. Preserve the existing source-before-body handling.
